stem: Each of the 40 students at a language institute studies French, German or both. Of these students, 25 study French and 22 study German, and 7 study both languages. If a student who studies exactly one of the two languages is selected at random, what is the probability that the student studies French?
solution: Students who study only French: \(25 - 7 = 18\). Students who study only German: \(22 - 7 = 15\). (Check: \(18 + 15 + 7 = 40\).)
So \(18 + 15 = 33\) students study exactly one language, and the probability is \(\frac{18}{33} = \frac{6}{11}\).

explanation.A: Correct. 18 students study only French and 15 study only German, so the probability is \(\frac{18}{33} = \frac{6}{11}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{25}{40}\), the probability that a student selected from all 40 students studies French, ignoring the condition.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{18}{40}\); the numerator is right, but the student is selected from the 33 students who study exactly one language, not from all 40.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{25}{33}\), which uses all 25 French students in the numerator; the 7 who study both languages are not among the students who study exactly one.

verify:
fo, go = 25 - 7, 22 - 7
assert fo + go + 7 == 40 and fo + go == 33
p = Rational(fo, fo + go)
assert p == Rational(6, 11)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
